hypotheses.claim: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms, a multiplicative-gated rank-power ruin score that weights route fill-ratio and route-distance exposure (both normalized by within-instance scale) and raises its rank exponent with stagnation_ratio will lower mean tour length below the current SBS 15.9986, with the largest per-instance gains concentrated in the weakest regimes (capacity_level=tight, size=100, spatial=clustered, depot_style=eccentric), because removing near-capacity and long-route nodes creates the highest-value reinsertion recombinations there while stagnation escalation prevents premature convergence at the ~2-3 ms first_feasible anchor.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve the single hook `score_ruin_nodes` into a capacity-tightness-aware multiplicative gating + rank-power ruin priority: score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i| / scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)), where gate_load emphasises nodes on high-fill-ratio routes (capacity_level=tight regimes), gate_rdist emphasises nodes on long/geometrically stretched routes (size=100 + eccentric depot), and the exponent p escalates from ~1.0 (intensification, low stagnation) to ~2.0-2.5 (diversification, high stagnation_ratio) so the anytime LNS keeps a monotone improving anytime_curve within the 500 ms deadline.
